answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Two prior experiments (memory_31 and memory_86) demonstrated that signup simplification and shortened onboarding drove durable lifts in activation and completion. These are directly applicable to the current decline. Verifying memory_31 and memory_86 will confirm the magnitude and durability of prior gains before scaling. While memory_73 (promotional pricing) addresses competitive pressure, it risks margin erosion in a price war and conflicts with long-term qualified revenue maximization. Memory_57 (referral) works well for existing customers but won't reverse the activation/onboarding declines. Memory_44 (enterprise sales) is valuable but requires build time we don't have this week. Simplifying onboarding addresses the measured QoQ decline directly, can be deployed quickly, and aligns with proven levers. Activation messaging (memory_91) could complement this but onboarding friction is the upstream problem.
